response.sql: WITH linked AS (SELECT o.orderbase, f.feerate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink), bench AS (SELECT AVG(feerate) AS b FROM linked), ch AS (SELECT orderbase, AVG(feerate) AS avg_rate FROM linked WHERE orderbase IS NOT NULL GROUP BY orderbase) SELECT AVG(ch.avg_rate) AS mean_avg_fee_rate, AVG(ch.avg_rate - bench.b) AS mean_excess_over_benchmark FROM ch CROSS JOIN bench WHERE ch.avg_rate > bench.b

assumptions.assumption: The benchmark is the average feerate over all fee records linked to an order (a record-level average, not an average of the channel averages). Null feerates are ignored.
Orders with a null orderbase are not treated as a channel, but their fees still count toward the benchmark.
orders.recordvault is unique per order, so the join does not duplicate fee rows.
If no channel is above the benchmark, the query returns one row with NULLs.
